head: 9d6cc4f040a78822b20070a3d8a729ee0b82d8de
claim: A LAN pairing server now listens only on the addresses it offered the phone, not on every interface of the computer

steps.start: Worktree at the LAN bind fix commit with the packages built (packages/discover/dist newer than its source). This computer had one LAN address (192.168.1.144), one Tailscale address and Docker bridge addresses; no pairing server was running.
steps: Read the verify skill and the discover-lan-bind feature recipe.
Wrote a Node consumer in a scratch directory outside the repository that imports reach and routes from @byokit/discover and reads this computer's addresses with routes().
Ran the consumer with node; it called reach({ port, via: 'lan' }) on a free port and printed the bind list and the dial URLs.
Started one node:http server on each address in the bind list on that port, and dialed each address (each answered HTTP 204).
Dialed 127.0.0.1 on the same port, an address the phone was not offered (connection refused).
Closed those servers and listened on 127.0.0.1 on the same port (accepted).
Called reach({ port, via: 'lan', interfaces: {} }) to exercise the no-address error case and printed the error it raised.
Saved the consumer output as discover-lan-bind.txt.
steps.result: The output shows reach via LAN returning bind ['192.168.1.144'] and the URL ws://192.168.1.144:41757, with no wildcard. The bind address answered HTTP 204, the unoffered 127.0.0.1 connect was refused (ECONNREFUSED), and the port could then be taken on loopback. The no-address case printed 'no LAN address; connect to a network or choose Tailscale'. The run exited 0.

verdicts.seen: Read all 9 entries in the capture. The bind is 192.168.1.144:41757, which is the only LAN URL offered (ws://192.168.1.144:41757). Dialing that address returns HTTP 204, while dialing 127.0.0.1:41757 (not offered) returns ECONNREFUSED. The Tailscale address of this computer is not in the bind list, and the error case confirms the no-LAN path. The outcome names one part, so parts is empty. The capture shows the outcome, so the result is correct.
